title: Lesson 89: Your Roadmap: The Next 90 Days of Learning and Building
description: Tests what each 30-day arc has to produce, where a rule that cannot have exceptions belongs, and the test that shows whether the workflow can be handed to somebody else.

questions.question: An architect has nine weeks of calendar room and a case-triage workflow she has already chosen. Her plan for the first 30 days lists a framework evaluation, a vector database comparison and three vendor whitepapers. Which closing number is missing from that arc?
options: A held-out pass rate against a measured baseline
A cost per unit and override rate measured on live cases
An approval with conditions from a reviewer who can say no
A runbook naming the escalation path and the on-call owner
questions.explanation: Arc one asks whether the workflow produces a number at all, and the number that closes it is a held-out pass rate against a measured baseline. Cost per unit and override rate belong to arc two, while the approval and the runbook belong to arc three. An arc spent comparing tools produces an opinion rather than a measurement.

questions.question: A team's service agent must never write to the billing object, and a review has just found that the rule was written as one strongly worded line in the system prompt. Where does the lesson say a rule like that belongs?
options: In the system prompt, restated once per session so it stays salient
In the evaluation set, as a case that scores the behavior after the fact
The rules that cannot have exceptions belong in hooks, deny rules and tests, because the harness runs them whether or not the model decides to cooperate
In the design packet, so that the next reviewer knows the rule existed
questions.explanation: The lesson splits instructions into non-deterministic ones the model reads and deterministic ones the harness executes every time, which covers hooks, deny rules and managed settings. A rule that must never happen cannot rest on the model deciding to cooperate on a given turn. If you keep rewriting an instruction to make it stick, that is evidence it belongs in the deterministic column.

questions.question: A builder wants to know whether the agent she built can survive her moving to another team next quarter. Which check does the lesson name as the cheap test that most teams fail?
options: The held-out split scores above the threshold written in the packet
The evaluation suite runs on a schedule whether or not anyone is watching
The decision records state what was rejected as well as what was chosen
Somebody else runs the workflow for a week, with you reachable but not present
questions.explanation: The lesson calls the handoff test cheap and notes that most teams fail it: somebody else runs the workflow for a week, with you reachable but not present. Every other option is a real part of the evidence trail, but none of them shows whether a second person can operate the system. A plan with no handoff step was a personal project with a deadline.
